stem: Which substrate does Complex IV act on?
rationale: The products are 4 oxidized cytochrome c molecules, 2 water molecules, and 4 protons pumped into the intermembrane space.

stem: What substance is required by the β subunits in ATP synthase?
rationale: ADP and P_i are taken up sequentially by the \beta subunits to form ATP, which is expelled as the rotating \gamma subunit squeezes each \beta subunit in turn and changes its conformation.

stem: What substance is ADP/ATP converted into during work performance?
rationale: When work is performed, ATP is converted to ADP. More respiration occurs when ATP is converted to ADP.

stem: What substance does the ADP/ATP transporter facilitate the movement of?
rationale: The ADP/ATP transporter facilitates entry of cytosolic ADP into and ATP out of the mitochondrion. The ADP/ATP transporter can become rate limiting.

stem: In which structure is thermogenin found?
rationale: Thermogenin, or uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1), is a physiologic uncoupler found in brown adipose tissue.
citation: chapter_13_the_respiratory_chain_and_oxidative_phosphorylation — The Respiratory Chain & Oxidative Phosphorylation > MANY POISONS INHIBIT THE RESPIRATORY CHAIN

stem: What substance is transported by uncouplers across the mitochondrial membrane?
rationale: Uncouplers such as dinitrophenol are amphipathic and increase the permeability of the lipoid inner mitochondrial membrane to protons. Physiologic uncouplers such as UCP1 are membrane-spanning proteins that have a similar effect.

rationale: Glutamate dehydrogenase is an intramitochondrial enzyme that uses NADPH.

rationale: NADH is produced continuously in the cytosol during glycolysis by glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase.
